headline: Spain went to war in July, Berlin hosted the Olympics in August, and a British king resigned in December
texture: The Spanish Army of Africa launched a coup against the Republic on July 17 and the country split. The first Francoist concentration camps opened two days later. Robert Capa took The Falling Soldier on September 5. German troops had walked back into the Rhineland in March, in breach of Versailles, and no government did anything about it.

Berlin opened the Summer Olympics on August 1 with the first live television coverage of a games, and Jesse Owens won the hundred metres two days later in front of a government that had explanations ready. Garmisch-Partenkirchen had held the winter games in February. Roosevelt was reelected on November 3 by the widest margin in a century.

Edward VIII signed the instrument of abdication on December 10 and Parliament passed the act the next day, after eleven months as king. The BBC launched a regular high-definition television service in November to a few hundred sets in London. The Crystal Palace burned down on November 30. Rudyard Kipling died in January, Maxim Gorky in June, and Federico Garcia Lorca was shot by Nationalist forces in August.

notes: Research pass July 2026. No prices section: the three price series all start later. Lorca and Pirandello carry no date because the source lists them as undated sub-entries. The Rhineland fact carries no date for the same reason, the source mentioning it only in the year summary. Edward VIII's eleven months as king, Roosevelt's margin being the widest in a century, and John Gilbert's career ending with sound are general knowledge rather than claims from the year pages.
